steps.title: Prepare Metabolomics Dataset
steps.instruction: Load the Miller et al 2015 dataset and clean the data by removing metabolite annotation columns and non-numeric entries.

substeps.instruction: Load CTD R package (v1.0.0) and the Miller2015 dataset.
Extract metabolite columns (those starting with 'IEM_') into a matrix.
Create diagnosis-patient mappings for cohorts: mcc, arg, cit, cob, ga, gamt, msud, mma, otc, pa, pku, tmhle, and ref.
Remove the diagnosis row and any x-compounds (rows starting with 'x -') from the matrix.
Convert all matrix elements to numeric format.

steps.title: Generate Pathway Maps
steps.instruction: Use the CTDext package to visualize patient perturbation data on curated pathway maps.

substeps.instruction: Install and load CTDext R package (v1.0.0).
Create an output directory named './pathwayVis'.
Retrieve the list of pathway maps using pathway.ListMaps_metabolon().
Generate a pathway map for a specific patient (e.g., 'IEM_1023') on the 'allPathways' map using plot.pathwayMap().

steps.title: Perform LOOCV Disease-Specific Network Analysis
steps.instruction: Estimate the probability and significance of patient-specific metabolite perturbations across different network learning paradigms.

substeps.instruction: Set tuning parameters: p0 = 0.1, p1 = 0.9, thresholdDiff = 0.01, and kmx = 15.
Iterate through three network types: 'ind' (latent embedding + pruning), 'noPruning' (latent embedding, no pruning), and 'noLatent' (no latent embedding or pruning).
For each disease model (cit, msud, mma, pa, pku) and fold, load the corresponding network and precomputed node rankings from CTDext.
Calculate p-values from z-score data using 2*pnorm(abs(i), lower.tail = FALSE).
For each patient, identify the top kmx perturbed metabolites and calculate encoding lengths using mle.getPtBSbyK and mle.getEncodingLength.
Save results as RData files in './loocv/loocv_[type]_runCTD/'.

steps.title: Evaluate Model Performance (Figure 3)
steps.instruction: Calculate ROC-AUCs and visualize CTD scores across diagnostic categories.

substeps.instruction: Load the LOOCV results for the 5 disease models and 3 network types.
Calculate the best bits for each patient: max(d.score) - log2(nrow(pt_data)).
Use the pROC package to calculate ROC-AUCs for the models.
Generate barplots of CTD signals using gridExtra.

steps.title: Analyze Individual Patient Signatures (Figure S1)
steps.instruction: Interpret disease signatures for selected representative patients and visualize their most connected modules.

substeps.instruction: Select representative patients: IEM_1017 (Citrullinemia), IEM_1058 (MSUD), IEM_1051 (MMA), IEM_1093 (PA), and IEM_1105 (PKU).
Load the pruned network for the patient's specific disease and fold.
Identify the top kmx (15) perturbed metabolites.
Compute node ranks using singleNode.getNodeRanksN and determine the most compressed subset of nodes.
Plot the resulting igraph object, scaling edge width by 50 * abs(weight).

steps.title: Conduct Power Analysis Simulation (Figure 4)
steps.instruction: Perform a power analysis using three simulated 50-node networks with 10%, 30%, and 60% connectedness.

substeps.instruction: Build three undirected networks (net1, net2, net3) with edge weights of 1.
Enumerate all possible node subsets of size 5 (approx. 2.1 million) and count edges using induced_subgraph.
Run CTD probability estimation for these subsets using a cluster (parallelized in chunks of 10,000).
Sample 2,500 node subsets equally across 11 edge-count categories (0 to 10 edges).
Estimate permutation-based p-values by drawing 2,000 random permutations of the d.score.
Calculate and plot the power and specificity of CTD upper-bound estimates.

steps.title: Compare Feature Selection Methods (Table 5)
steps.instruction: Compare CTD feature selection against Z-score and FCFSN (InfoMap, WalkTrap, GMO) using PLS regression.

substeps.instruction: Filter metabolites based on a fill rate > 0.80.
Implement Z-score selection (abs mean z-score > 2) and CTD selection (metabolites present in >50% of patients' optimal subsets).
Implement FCFSN algorithm using the provided whichRtoSelect, prunedIGraph, and fsfcn functions.
Build PLS regression models using the 'pls' package, including the CTD score as a covariate.
Calculate variable importance using the caret package and compute AUC for each model.

steps.title: Perform Topological Pathway Enrichment (Figure 5)
steps.instruction: Compare CTD with other enrichment methods (CePa, PRS, SPIA, DEGraph, ORA, GSEA) using TCGA breast cancer data.

substeps.instruction: Normalize TCGA RNA-seq data using DESeq2 and filter for breast cancer subtypes (lumA, lumB, her2, basal) and normal samples.
Build a KEGG pathway catalogue using the graphite package.
For each subtype, perform differential expression analysis using limma (deAna).
Run CTD enrichment: build disease and reference networks using huge (glasso, lambda=0.1), prune the network, and calculate p-values.
Run comparison methods: CePa (betweenness), PRS (nperm=1000), SPIA (fisher combine), DEGraph (fishersMethod), ORA (phyper), and GSEA (fgsea).
FDR-correct p-values and rank pathways to generate the final comparison plot.

steps.title: Perform Metabolomics Set Enrichment (MSEA/ORA)
steps.instruction: Apply ORA and MSEA to the Miller et al 2015 dataset for 5 diagnostic categories.

substeps.instruction: For ORA: use stat.getORA_Metabolon with a z-score threshold of 2 for selected patients.
For MSEA: filter metabolites by 80% fill rate, define diagnostic indicators, and run stat.getMSEA_Metabolon using the 'Metabolon' knowledgebase.

steps.title: Validate Network Specificity via Surrogate Profiles
steps.instruction: Construct LOOCV data matrices using surrogate profiles to test the impact of network specificity on probability assignment.

substeps.instruction: Separate data into cohorts (Citrullinemia, MMA, PKU, and Reference).
Generate surrogate profiles using data.surrogateProfiles with 1 standard deviation around real patient profiles.
Learn network folds using huge (glasso, lambda=0.25) and prune using graph.naivePruning.
Calculate probabilities for top K (5, 10, 15, 20) perturbed metabolites across disease-specific, reference, and random networks.
Plot the Log2 ratio of probabilities relative to the random network.
